property_summary: Reference C ensures that after any sequence of Put and Collect calls, the sum of all Acc[user].balance exactly equals total Ether received minus total Ether paid out, while the buggy M decreases balance on Put, violating this invariant for some deposit amount.

For any user who deposits then collects a partial amount, the collected amount must not exceed the user's balance before collection, but the buggy Put reduces balance causing subsequent Collect to revert on 'sub_uint256' assertion when the user attempts to collect more than the reduced balance.

For any user who deposits Ether and then attempts to collect any amount less than or equal to their balance before the deposit, the collection must succeed (not revert), but the buggy Put decreases balance causing Collect to revert due to insufficient balance.
For any caller, after a Put deposit, immediately calling Collect(0) (or any amount <= balance) should not revert, but the buggy sub_uint256 makes it revert because balance decreases.
For any user who deposits, the user's balance after the deposit must be at least the deposited amount, but the buggy Put decreases balance, making the balance smaller than the deposited amount.

For every call to Put, the recorded unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp at the time of the call. The buggy version can set it strictly lower than the supplied _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp, violating the invariant.

After any Put call, the unlockTime must equal the maximum of the supplied _unlockTime and the block timestamp; the buggy version always sets unlockTime to block.timestamp, violating when _unlockTime is in the future.

After a Put call with a future _unlockTime, the stored unlockTime must be greater than the current block.timestamp; the bug sets it to block.timestamp, so when _unlockTime > block.timestamp the buggy unlockTime is not in the future.

After any Put call, unlockTime must equal the supplied _unlockTime when it is >= block.timestamp, and be >= block.timestamp always; the mutant always sets unlockTime to block.timestamp, so for future _unlockTime values the stored unlockTime is strictly less than the parameter.

For any Put call, if the supplied _unlockTime is strictly greater than block.timestamp, then the stored unlockTime must equal _unlockTime; the mutant always stores block.timestamp, violating this when a future unlock is requested.

After any call to Put, the caller's balance in contract C must increase by exactly the Ether amount sent, but the mutant fails this because it omits the balance update while still logging the sent value.
After any call to Put, summing the collected value for a caller should equal their account balance, but the mutant logs sent value without updating balance, so the collected-to-balance link breaks.

After a successful Put, Acc[caller].balance must equal the returned balance from a subsequent Collect of the same amount, but the mutant breaks this because it never updates Acc[caller].balance in Put.

After any call to Put with a positive msg.value and an unlockTime in the past, the contract's ETH balance increases but the caller's Acc.balance does not, so a subsequent Collect of any valid amount from the same caller in the same transaction must revert on the buggy version but succeed on the reference.
A subsequent Collect of at most the sent amount must succeed after a Put with a past unlockTime, but the mutant's missing balance update causes Collect to revert.

The total balance recorded for each user must equal the sum of all Ether sent to the contract by that user; the bug sets the balance to only the latest sent amount, breaking this invariant when the user sends multiple payments.

For any two consecutive deposits from the same sender, the final balance recorded in Acc must be the sum of both deposited amounts; the bug sets balance to only the second deposit, breaking this additivity.

After any sequence of calls to Put from a single sender, the balance recorded in Acc for that sender must equal the sum of all Ether sent via Put; the bug resets balance to the latest sent amount, violating this summation invariant.

After any number of deposits (Put calls) by the same sender, the recorded balance must be at least the value of the single largest deposit they sent; the bug resets balance to the latest deposit only, so when a smaller deposit follows a larger one, the recorded balance becomes strictly less than the max ever deposited.

For any sender, after any sequence of Put calls, the recorded balance must never be less than the total Ether deposited by that sender in non-fallback calls; the bug resets balance to the latest deposit, causing the recorded balance to fall below the cumulative sum when a Put with zero Ether follows a previous Put with positive Ether.
After a Put operation, the unlockTime of the caller should be greater than or equal to block.timestamp. The correct contract enforces this, while the mutant allows unlockTime to be set in the past.
After a Put, the caller's unlockTime must be >= block.timestamp, but the mutant lets it be < block.timestamp, making Collect possible earlier than intended.

For any caller, immediately after a successful Put with an _unlockTime in the past, the caller's unlockTime returned by Acc[caller] must be equal to the current block.timestamp, but the mutant sets it to the passed past _unlockTime instead.

After Put with any _unlockTime, a subsequent Put call with a smaller _unlockTime must not cause the caller's unlockTime to decrease, but the mutant allows the second Put's _unlockTime to overwrite the first's, reducing unlockTime.

For any caller, after two consecutive Put operations with arbitrary unlock times, the final unlockTime must be at least as large as the current block.timestamp, but the mutant can set it to a smaller past value from the second call.

For any sequence of calls through Put, the balance of an account after a Put call must equal its balance before plus the msg.value sent, but with the nonReentrant_ modifier removed a re-entrant caller can inflate its balance during the same Put execution.

For any reentrant caller that performs a Collect within its receive function during a Put, the reference contract's nonReentrant_ modifier on Put prevents the reentrant call and the balance update is correct, while the buggy contract allows reentrancy, causing acc.balance to underflow or become inconsistent with the deposited amount.

After a Put call, the caller's Acc balance must equal the previous balance plus msg.value, but the missing nonReentrant_ modifier in the mutant allows a reentrant call during LogFile.AddMessage to inflate the balance beyond this invariant.

After a Put call, the caller's Acc balance is at most the previous balance plus msg.value; the buggy version without nonReentrant_ allows a reentrant call during the external LogFile.AddMessage to inflate the balance beyond this bound.

For any reentrant caller that calls Put and then, during the external LogFile.AddMessage call, calls Collect to drain its balance, the reference contract's nonReentrant modifier prevents the reentrant Collect from executing, so the balance after the subsequent Collect (outside the reentrant context) is the initial balance plus msg.value minus the collected amount; the buggy contract allows the reentrant Collect to execute inside Put's external call, leaving the final balance equal to the initial balance (zero net change) regardless of msg.value.

After a call to Put, the value of the unlocked time stored for the caller (Acc[caller].unlockTime) is always strictly greater than the block timestamp at the time of the call, but the bug allows a re-entrant call that overwrites it with a smaller value or zero.

For any caller, after a single Put, the caller's balance can only increase or stay the same; the buggy reentrancy lock allows a re-entrant Put during Collect's external call to reset the balance, reducing it below the pre-call value.

For any caller, the number of successful Collect operations that move Ether out of the contract measured by the total Ether balance decrease cannot exceed the number of successful Put operations by the same caller; the buggy missing reentrancy lock allows a re-entrant call during the external call in Collect to double-spend the balance, causing a greater decrease than the caller's net deposits.
Reentrancy via a Put call during Collect's external send resets the Collect caller's balance, allowing them to drain funds beyond their own deposits.
After a call to Put(...) succeeds, locked_ is false in the correct contract; in the buggy contract locked_ remains true, causing the next nonReentrant call to revert.

After two consecutive successful calls to Put with the same sender, the second call succeeds in the reference but always reverts in the buggy version because locked_ is never released after the first call.

Any address can successfully call Put() at least once, and on the reference contract a second Put() from the same address also succeeds, but on the buggy contract the second Put() always reverts because the lock is never released.

For any sender who has successfully called Put at least once, a subsequent call to Put will succeed on the reference contract, but on the buggy contract it will always revert because the reentrancy lock is never released.
After any successful Put call, a subsequent Put call by the same sender succeeds in the reference but always reverts in the mutant because the lock is never released.
